author: Shurtz, Ammon; Richardson, Christian; Richardson, Stephen D.
title: MekongPhon: A Large-Scale Parallel IPA Corpus for Lao and Khmer
scope: Authors explicitly state that all data, code and pretrained models are publicly released to support future research and development (ACL Anthology record, abstract); ClippyFirst uses the pinned corpus for non-redistributive research, rule-discovery and comparative diagnostics. Paper reports 367,388 Lao orthography–IPA sentence pairs and a 6,039-entry seed lexicon derived from Kerr (1972), with a two-author 500-entry review (97.2% sample accuracy; reviewers are proficient L2 speakers, not native speakers). Pinned GitHub snapshot f80f6c1840c4818b51e05f2e00cded4701a5b662 contains 6,319 lexicon rows (6,316 unique spellings), 6,219 train rows (lao_train.csv SHA-256 2d0f68989009620980ced3386f11a640e6167404308eeb6a79efc52bc8e40ee0) and 100 eval rows; three duplicate spellings occur in train and there is no train/eval overlap. Sentence pairs are generated by longest-match trie lookup over OPUS text (NLLB/Paracrawl/OpenSubtitles); held-out evaluation is dictionary-seeded, not independent sentence transcription or ClippyFirst gold. The current ClippyFirst diagnostic consumes only the word-level seed-lexicon train split, not OPUS-derived sentence pairs; The upstream snapshot's missing root LICENSE remains a provenance fact. Independent reuse of SEAlang/OPUS outside MekongPhon remains governed by their own terms. The repository owner confirms full rights for all MekongPhon components in the authorized project use; this supersedes the preliminary UNKNOWN status and is not an independent legal opinion.

author: Zhu, Jian; Zhang, Cong; Jurgens, David
title: ByT5 model for massively multilingual grapheme-to-phoneme conversion
scope: Interspeech 2022; multilingual ByT5 G2P, code and model release at https://github.com/lingjzhu/CharsiuG2P. At inspected commit 0c929390759fb94f8ecdfc05cc0bc5f2ff2dc0f4, sources/info/wikipron/lao_laoo_broad_info.txt points to CUNY-CL WikiPron lao_laoo_broad.tsv and declares Apache-2.0 for that source metadata. A recursive inspection of the same commit's full tree found no Lao file in data/train, data/dev or data/test and no Lao entry in the model's checked-in split inventories; Khmer is present. Therefore the presence of Lao source metadata does not establish Lao model training or evaluation, and CharsiuG2P is not currently a supervised Lao benchmark candidate on this revision.

author: Osatananda, Varisa
title: Tone in Vientiane Lao
scope: One Vientiane variety in Vientiane Prefecture; five lexical tones, final stress, and an analysis in which each syllable has underlying lexical tone rather than tone being mechanically derived by orthographic rules. Important competing analysis and dialect-specific caution; not a replacement rule table for the project's declared Vientiane profile.

author: Phissamay, Phonpasit; Dalolay, Valaxay; Chanhsililath, Chitaphone; Silimasak, Oulaiphone; Hussain, Sarmad; Durrani, Nadir

scope: Working Papers 2004–2007, pp. 291–296; reports a rule-based orthographic syllable identification technique with more than 98% results, but the accessible paper does not establish a reproducible benchmark split or a pronunciation evaluation. It targets line breaking, not lexical word segmentation or IPA accuracy. Used as structural comparison only.

author: Phatthiyaphaibun, Wannaphong
title: LaoNLP: Lao language Natural Language Processing
scope: Pinned upstream repository commit a914f64e38ff24d67d32e37db40dad5c368ea602 (2026-09-23); package code is Apache-2.0. syllable_tokenize is a regex model based on Phissamay et al. for orthographic syllable segmentation/line breaking; its semivowel class includes U+0EBC LAO SEMIVOWEL SIGN LO, but this is not a validated phonological segmentation or LOC Note 10 source-role model. word_tokenize uses PyThaiNLP Trie and maximum matching over lao_words(), a union of Lao-Dictionary.txt, lo_spellcheck_dict.txt, lao-wannaphong.txt and wiktionary-20210720.txt. This algorithm is not the LOC Note 9 shortest-standalone-written-form/loanword rule. The composite dictionary has mixed per-file licenses and one file with no license notice; not imported into ClippyFirst runtime. The standalone syllable tokenizer code and bundled datasets must be assessed separately. Neither tokenizer nor dictionary is IPA gold.

author: E-Government Center, Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications of Laos
title: Lao-English dictionary dataset bundled with LaoNLP

Pronunciation is Latin romanization, not IPA. Mixed phrases and inconsistent Type values mean this is not lexical-boundary gold. Not imported into runtime. Preserve separate MIT notice if redistributed.

author: Ylönen, Tatu; Wiktionary contributors
title: Machine-readable Lao dictionary extracted from English Wiktionary
scope: Postprocessed JSONL download is based on enwiktionary dump 2026-10-01, extracted 2026-10-30 with Wiktextract 19f9a30 and WikitextProcessor 6f96ddf. Full JSONL parse: 2,751 records, 2,378 unique word forms, 2,320 unique IPA-bearing forms, 2,691 records with IPA and 5,392 IPA values (2,695 Vientiane-labelled, 2,695 Luang Prabang-labelled, 2 unlabelled). A deterministic 100-form sample was selected by ascending 32-bit FNV-1a over Unicode code points; 100/100 raw page revisions dated on or before dump date directly invoke lo-pron. Manifest: data/evidence/kaikki_lao_ipa_provenance_sample_2026-11-09.csv. Sample evidence only; do not treat all normalized IPA as exclusively generated by lo-pron or as independent gold. author: Lew, S.
title: A linguistic analysis of the Lao writing system and its suitability for minority language orthographies
scope: Writing Systems Research, pp. 25–40. Analyzes Lao grapheme–phoneme correspondences and orthographic structure; emphasizes dialectal differences in lexicon, vowels and especially tone. Useful for script-to-phoneme architecture, not an independent word-level IPA corpus.

author: Lao Language Specific Peculiarities document authors
title: Language Specific Peculiarities Document for Lao as Spoken in Laos 1. Dialects
scope: Documents major Lao dialect differences in pronunciation and tone; notes that ໃ and ໄ are pronounced the same in Vientiane but differently in Luang Prabang. Secondary language-resource profile; use for dialect boundary checks, not as a complete phonological grammar.

author: Enfield, N. J.
title: Word in Lao
scope: Describes syllables grouped into feet; each foot includes one stressed syllable bearing contrastive tone plus one or more unstressed phonologically dependent syllables. Grammatical-word and phonological-word boundaries do not always coincide. Useful for phrase/word segmentation caution, not a simple grapheme-level rule.

author: Davis, Garry W.
title: The Story of Lao r
scope: Discusses historical grapheme ຣ and loss of /r/: historical /r/ became /h/ under some conditions and /l/ elsewhere, and clusters were lost; loans from Pali-Sanskrit, Khmer and Thai complicate modern spellings. Supports conservative lexeme/context exceptions rather than a universal single-value assumption.

author: Sengsoulin, Bounleuth
title: Pali and Sanskrit words in Lao language
scope: Discusses Indic-origin vocabulary in Lao. Use as a separate lexical/orthographic profile lead; do not assign modern spoken-Lao IPA from etymological spellings alone.

author: Yanagimura, Y.
title: Contextual Tonal Variations in Vientiane Lao
scope: Studies all 25 bitonal sequences from five lexical tones in one Vientiane variety using recorded productions and F0 contours. Reports stronger carryover than anticipatory effects and context-dependent tonal realization. Published text can guide prosodic caution; this is not a grapheme-to-lexical-tone mapping table.

author: Lee, Jackson L. et al.
title: Massively Multilingual Pronunciation Modeling with WikiPron
scope: Wiktionary-derived pronunciation lexicon and G2P resource. Lao-specific coverage, source provenance, dialect and license need separate verification before use; generated or imported entries must not be assumed to be independently authored Lao IPA.

author: Nguyen-Tien, Ha; Palongve, Thongphan; Nguyen-Quy, Cuong; Le-Trung, Kien
title: Semi-Automatic Construction and Benchmarking of a Word-Segmented Corpus for Lao Using LLMs and Transformer Models
scope: Published in Informatica 49 (2025), 379–394. The journal article page states CC BY 3.0 for articles; this licence applies to the article text, not automatically to the separately released corpus or underlying source-web texts. Appendix B describes minimal orthographic units carrying lexical/grammatical meaning, smallest-consistent segmentation, context-sensitive decisions, function words/particles, productive morphemes and lexicalized compounds. The paper reports native annotator review, a linguist adjudicator and 5% double annotation (500 sentences; segmentation F1 0.80). title: HVULao_NLP: A Word-Segmented Lao Corpus with Optional POS Tags, version 2
scope: Mendeley Data version 2 lists CC BY 4.0 and provides 10,000 training plus 1,000 test sentences. The associated paper's ethical statement says the source websites explicitly allow text reuse for research and non-commercial purposes; this statement is a separate restriction/evidence boundary and the dataset-level CC BY 4.0 label does not independently establish commercial rights in the underlying government/news/institutional source texts. The paper's Table 2 identifies seven source domains and aggregate sentence counts, not item-level sentence-to-URL permissions. Research comparator only; require source-item locators and rights review before importing or commercially redistributing any source text. No corpus data or model imported.

author: Lao Language Specific Peculiarities document authors
title: Language Specific Peculiarities Document for Lao as Spoken in Laos — special handling of spelling
scope: Section 3 (pp. 2–3): describes the post-1975 phonetic spelling reforms; says ຣ was reintroduced for recently borrowed foreign words, while Pali/Sanskrit borrowings use ລ instead; gives Paris and Russia as recent-loan examples and notes spelling variation. This is source-specific orthographic evidence for origin-sensitive lexeme metadata, not a complete lexical segmentation rule or proof that loan origin can be inferred from spelling alone.

author: CrossAsia Digital / Digital Library of Lao Manuscripts
title: DLLM Collection — Lao Orthography and Romanisation
scope: The DLLM cataloguing convention documents historical Indic phonemes in some Pali/Sanskrit loanword spellings (e.g. ສັພ from Sanskrit śabda, ນິພພານ from Pali nibbāna, ເຖຣີ from Pali therī, ສູຕ from Sanskrit sūtra), while commonly used Indic loans may follow modern Lao pronunciation (e.g. ນະຄອນ, ທັມມາດ). This is a collection-specific cataloguing/romanisation convention, not a national standard or LOC word-boundary gold; the page states copyright and no open-data licence was identified, so no table or dataset was copied.

author: Wilson, Brian Eugene; Campbell, Robert Martin; Unicode Consortium; International Business Machines Corporation
title: ICU Lao word-break dictionary (laodict.txt)
scope: Pinned ICU commit bf835bad36a09828051dd8cc6f58bb62bac93fde; Git blob SHA-1 8eb43185e9ab6d00afe0f80e17891e33af976f06; header identifies a 2020-11-22 source snapshot, Unicode/IBM notices and BSD-style redistribution terms. The referenced upstream repository rober42539/lao-dictionary currently displays takeover/defacement content and its current LICENSE.txt redirects to an unrelated site; do not fetch from that mutable upstream. The pinned ICU copy is the reviewed source candidate.

author: American Library Association; Library of Congress
title: ALA-LC Lao Romanization Table
scope: Historical 1997 version of the LOC Lao Romanization Table. The current LOC Romanization Tables index lists Lao (2012) as the current table and 1997 only under earlier versions; LOC says earlier versions are for reference only and should not be used in current cataloging. The available retrieval text exposes only title/version metadata; the 1997 example glyphs were not independently inspected in this audit, so no Note 10 glyph example is asserted from this copy. The 2012 table remains the project's primary standard.

author: Library of Congress
title: ALA-LC Romanization Tables — current table index and version guidance
scope: The official index lists Lao (2012) as the current table and 1997 under earlier versions. LOC states earlier versions are for reference only and are not to be used in current cataloging; it instructs users to use the source documents rather than the PDF versions when copying data. This establishes version authority, not the contents of Note 9/10 beyond the linked Lao source document.

author: Library of Congress
title: Source Documents for Romanization Tables
scope: LOC states that Microsoft Word source files are the source documents from which ALA-LC tables are created and explicitly instructs users to use these Word source documents, not PDF versions, when copying data. The Lao entry links to https://www.loc.gov/catdir/cpso/romanization/lao.doc. author: UNGEGN Working Group on Romanization Systems
title: Report of the Working Group on Romanization Systems: current status of UN romanization systems for geographical names (GEGN.2/2023/11/CRP.11)
scope: The report states that the Working Group had been invited to review a draft Lao Romanization System prepared by the National Geographic Department of the Lao PDR, had made recommendations, and wished to resume discussion with the Lao government to finalise it and consider it for UN adoption. This documents a draft/review stage, not approval or a finalized national standard.

author: United Nations Group of Experts on Geographical Names
title: UNGEGN Romanization Systems — current status
scope: The current UNGEGN index lists Lao version 4.0 dated 2013-09-24 among other language/script systems, and lists no later Lao version. The index is evidence of the currently listed UN system, not proof by itself of all domestic national policy.

title: Liste des noms de pays du GENUNG (GEGN.2/2025/171/CRP.171)
